disasters.summary: As of 12 November 2026, the notes found no reports dated that month. OCHA reported on 28 August 2026 that Panama and El Salvador declared nationwide states of emergency on 25 August to speed drought response through 2027. The IFRC projects more severe drought conditions from October 2026 to March 2027. In Panama's Dry Arc provinces, rainfall deficits have disrupted planting, reduced yields and raised basic food prices.

disasters.summary: A drought in East Africa and the Central Sahel started on 21 May 2026. A FEWS NET report from October 2026 says the Sahel rainy season is ending, with widespread rainfall deficits, most pronounced in Chad. South Sudan regions recorded rainfall below 60 percent of average. A JRC report from September 2026 describes degraded rangelands and lower crop and livestock output. The notes do not say whether drought continues in East Africa as of 12 November 2026.

disasters.summary: Drought in Central America began on 21 April 2026 and is linked to El Niño. Honduras declared a drought emergency on 19 August, and El Salvador declared a nationwide Red Alert on 25 August. Crop losses have been reported in several areas. As of 7 November 2026, the drought was ongoing, and sources expect effects to continue into 2027.

disasters.summary: Typhoon Cempaka (Typhoon No. 32) formed in the Pacific around 6 to 7 November 2026 and passed the Ogasawara Islands near Japan by 9 November. A JMA-based update of 11 November said it was moving east-northeast at 45 km/h and was expected to become extratropical far east of Japan by 12 November. The transition is not yet confirmed. The sources reviewed report no deaths, damage or evacuations in Japan.

disasters.summary: A flash flood struck Rasuwa district in Nepal's Bagmati Province on 26 August 2026, damaging settlements, markets, roads and hydropower facilities and affecting nearby districts. Authorities reported deaths, missing people and displaced people. The latest source found, an IFRC update dated 12 October 2026, says humanitarian needs continue and some road access remains limited.

disasters.summary: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, on 15 August 2026 (local time), causing deaths, injuries and building damage. BNPB reported 47 deaths and 101 injuries as of 16 August, with more than 5,000 people still displaced. Aftershocks have decreased, and monitoring of secondary hazards continues.

disasters.summary: Monsoon floods in Myanmar, alert issued 12 August 2026, followed heavy rain from late July that breached river embankments and submerged villages in several regions, including Ayeyarwady, Rakhine and Sagaing. As of the end of August 2026, about 600,000 people were reported affected by ongoing flooding. Floodwaters have receded in most central and southern townships. The sources found do not cover this flood after late August.

disasters.summary: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck Chocó department in Colombia on 10 August 2026, with its epicentre near San José del Palmar. The latest national balance cited is UNGRD's of 22 August 2026: 16 departments and 481 municipalities affected. Aftershocks were recorded after the mainshock. The notes do not say whether the disaster is over.

disasters.title: Afghanistan: Nuristan Flood
disasters.summary: Flash floods struck Nuristan province in eastern Afghanistan on 20 July 2026. Reports give 23 deaths and 125 injuries in Nuristan, with more than 100 people missing. Parun City, the provincial capital, and Mandol District were among the areas hit. The latest source found is UNICEF Flash Update #2, dated 29 July 2026. No later status was found.
